reported.title: E-stop polarity inverted: contactor runs while e-stop is pressed
reported.description: estopActive() at line 20 returns true when the pin reads HIGH, but the e-stop is active LOW (pressed = LOW), so the logic is inverted. With the e-stop held LOW, stableStop settles to LOW, stopped becomes false at line 69, and the else branches at lines 76-83 drive D5 HIGH; measured evidence shows 'D5 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required' and 'D5 was not LOW for 48 ms while required' in the rapid-press scenario. This makes the contactor energize during an emergency stop, the opposite of the required safe behavior. D5 was in the wrong state for 4842 ms across 31 interval(s), first at 100 ms: D5 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required (grace 100 ms).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D5 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D3 == 1; LOW when D3 == 0; within 100 ms (Contactor follows e-stop)

judge_input.spec:
- E-stop on D3 with INPUT_PULLUP, active LOW when pressed. Contactor coil on D5. Run request on D6 (pull-up).
- Contactor D5 must drop LOW when e-stop is held (D3 LOW), and run HIGH when e-stop is released.
- React within 100 ms of a settled e-stop level change.
- Settle the e-stop contact for 30 ms before counting a new trip.
- Print `hoist run=<0|1> trips=<n>` every 1100 ms.
- When e-stop is clear, keep the contactor available (HIGH) for hoist motion.
